merged.title: fix(editor): ship typed pvar layouts with installed tools
merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
Replaces #94 after rebuilding on the current master history.

Typed pvar edits could work in a source checkout but be ignored by installed editor tools, which do not carry the decompilation headers used by `class_layouts()`. Invalid packaged definitions fail explicitly instead of becoming a cached empty layout.

Also ignore the inherited descriptive class metadata Godot saves on instances, while preserving validation of gameplay fields. This fixes the installed-tools defect without changing PAL's existing 60 Hz gameplay selection. Novalis's historical `moveSpeed` field stores travel duration, so larger values make the platform slower.

Rebuilt as a focused seven-file patch on current master after the history rewrite; independent of the creator-map framework in #101.

merged.title: fix(port/rac1-ntsc): give FUN_0020db40's places one C, the grid's own
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
NTSC logged "two functions at … in overlay N: FUN_0020db40 and func_0020DB40; keeping the first" for overlays 12 to 18 and the executable.

The NTSC catalogue folds `FUN_0020db40` (the moby grid's block free) with its level copies, and two C functions claimed those places: the grid's own `func_0020DB40` in `hand/game_moby_grid.c`, which the grid updater calls, and a carry of PAL's level copy `func_L00_00251A78` (in `hand/functional/`) that hard-wires level 0's bitmap even when the executable's program runs it. This keeps the grid's own, as `func_0020DBA0` already serves `FUN_0020dba0`, and drops the carried copy with its rows in `hand.tsv`, `allow.tsv` and `fcheck.tsv`. Only the table calls that address, so play does not change; the address table loses its 20 duplicates.

merged.title: feat(port): optional fresh pad input and low-latency frames
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
- New setting `fresh_input` (drawer: Sound and game, off by default): the pad is read again right before each tick, so presses reach the game up to a tick sooner.
- New setting `low_latency_frames` (drawer: Graphics, off by default): frames between ticks are no longer held half a tick behind. With VSync the next tick starts on time; without VSync the half-tick freeze-then-jump is gone. Fewer frames queue for the display (Vulkan: fewest swapchain images and one frame in flight; OpenGL: glFinish after swap).
- Both are off by default because they shift when a press lands relative to the picture, so tricks timed by feel would land earlier. Game logic and the one pad read per tick are unchanged.
- Docs: SETTINGS.md, speedrun/REFERENCE.md, CONTROLLERS.md.

Tested: debug build, ctest (frontend_pacing has a new test; xcheck_tool fails on develop too), CI checks and launcher green on the fork. Not tested in game with the new switches.

merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
**Fix:** Before a switch to or from the main menu starts, the target page's animation for the Exit slot is temporarily swapped for Options', and restored once it ends. Exit merges into Options as the game's rows shrink, then is moved out of sight; on the way back it comes out of Options at its smallest and grows into its row with the other rows.

This fixes Exit vanishing after going back from a page (it settled on the off-screen frame, or the switch started before the swap), and it no longer drifts down into the footer or slides in from the left.

merged.title: fix(port): Exit and the player's language survive Quit Game
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
## Before
After a game was started and left with Quit Game from the pause menu, the title's main menu showed the Exit row with no text (only its frame), and the language went back to the one the port started with (English for most players), which was then remembered for the next run. Before entering a game, changing the language and Exit worked.

## After
After Quit Game the main menu has its Exit row (and any mods' rows) with their texts again, and the language stays the one the player chose.

- Quit Game reads the boot program back from the disc, and the port puts the executable's own data back in its place (rac1 `boot.c`), the main menu's page with it: the game's three rows again. `mod_ui.cpp` patched the page only once; it now keeps the rows it made and puts them back whenever the main menu is the game's three rows again (no new game memory is made).

opened.author: chistianh

**Title:** tools: expand li.s as SN's assembler does; PAL C for 27 functions it unblocks

### The tool change

GCC writes every float constant as `li.s $fN, value`. Retail's assembler, SN's `ps2eeas`, always builds the value in `$at`: `lui`, plus `ori` when the low half is not zero, then `mtc1`. The driver's GNU `as` does that only when the low half is zero. For any other value, at -G8, it puts the value in `.lit4` and loads it with one `lwc1 ...($gp)`. That is one word instead of three, plus a `$gp` access retail does not have. So no function with a float constant like 0.3 or 1.6 could match.

- I checked it on `ps2eeas` itself (`toolchain/sn-prodg-3.01/.../Ps2EeAs.exe`, 1.9.25) on test files: `li.s $f12, 0.08` becomes `lui $at, 0x3DA3; ori $at, $at, 0xD70B; mtc1 $at, $f12`.
- In the PAL text the `lui`/`ori`/`mtc1 $at` form appears 13,207 times.
